# Copilot instructions for Booked_Mic

Purpose: give Copilot sessions repository-specific context so generated changes and suggestions match build, test, and runtime expectations.

---

## Quick commands (where to run)

Root (general JavaScript tooling)
- Install root npm deps (if any): npm install

Flutter app (root):
- Install Dart/Flutter deps: flutter pub get
- Run (web debug): flutter run -d chrome
- Run on device/emulator: flutter run
- Build web: flutter build web
- Analyze (lint): flutter analyze
- Run tests (single file): flutter test test/path/to/test_file.dart
- Run full test suite: flutter test

Cloud Functions (functions/)
- Install deps: cd functions && npm install
- Lint: cd functions && npm run lint
- Build TypeScript: cd functions && npm run build
- Serve locally (emulators): cd functions && npm run serve
- Start functions shell: cd functions && npm run shell
- Deploy: cd functions && npm run deploy
- View logs: cd functions && npm run logs

Admin dashboard (admin-dashboard/)
- Install deps: cd admin-dashboard && npm install
- Start dev server: cd admin-dashboard && npm start
- Build: cd admin-dashboard && npm run build
- Run tests (single): cd admin-dashboard && npm test -- <filename-or-pattern>

Firebase emulators (project root)
- Start emulators used by local dev (Auth, Firestore, Functions, UI):
  firebase emulators:start --only auth,firestore,functions,ui

Note: Flutter web debug mode expects emulators on localhost:9099 (Auth) and 8080 (Firestore) per firebase.json.

---

## High-level architecture (big picture)

- Mobile / Web app (Flutter): main entry at lib/main.dart. Uses Provider for state; FirestoreProvider bridges UI to FirestoreService. Data models include Show (Lists), Performer, City. The app supports two roles: host and performer; AuthWrapper chooses the route.

- Backend (Firebase): Firestore (real-time DB), Firebase Auth, Cloud Functions (TypeScript) for privileged operations. Functions live in functions/src and are TypeScript-built -> lib. Functions use the v2 firebase-functions SDK (onCall, onDocumentUpdated) and admin SDK for FCM and Firestore updates.

- Admin Dashboard (React): in admin-dashboard/, built with react-scripts; hosting configured in firebase.json to serve admin-dashboard/build.

- Emulators: firebase.json configures auth (9099), firestore (8080), functions (5001) and emulator UI (4000). Single-project mode is enabled for local development.

---

## Key repository conventions and patterns

- Firestore collections and shapes:
  - Lists collection name: "Lists" (used by FirestoreService). Each list document contains a `spots` map and `signedUpUserIds` array.
  - Spots map keys: numeric string keys ("1","2",...) represent main list spots. Waitlist spots use keys like "W1","W2".
  - Bucket signups are stored under a subcollection `bucketSignups` on each list document.
  - Users document may contain `fcmTokens` (array) used by functions to send notifications.
  - Host code lookup uses `users` collection field `hostCode`.

- Firestore operations:
  - Use transactions (runTransaction) for atomic spot mutations, reorder and sign-up operations to avoid double-booking.
  - Use FieldValue.serverTimestamp() for createdAt/time fields.
  - When updating a show, FirestoreService strips non-updatable fields (userId, createdAt, spots, signedUpUserIds, id) before writing.

- Cloud Functions patterns:
  - TypeScript v2-style triggers (onCall, onDocumentUpdated) in functions/src/index.ts. Functions build with tsc (functions npm run build).
  - Notification flow: onListUpdateShiftSpots inspects before/after snapshots and composes an updates map, then updates Firestore and sends FCM via admin.messaging.sendEachForMulticast.
  - Node engine target is 22 (see functions/package.json). ESLint + @typescript-eslint used for linting.

- App-level behaviors:
  - The app loads a .env file (flutter_dotenv) and expects firebase_options.dart to exist (auto-generated by Firebase CLI or FlutterFire). Ensure .env is present in dev environments.
  - Quick Actions and HomeWidget integrations are present in lib/main.dart; HomeWidget uses an app group id 'group.bookedmic.app'.
  - Provider pattern: FirestoreProvider is registered as ChangeNotifier at app root. SettingsService is provided as a singleton via Provider.

---

## Where to look first for common tasks
- lib/services/firestore_service.dart — core DB logic and atomic transaction patterns
- functions/src/index.ts — server-side business logic and notification flows
- lib/main.dart — app initialization (Firebase, env, notification init, routes)
- firebase.json — emulator ports, hosting, and emulator UI settings
- pubspec.yaml — Flutter dependencies and dev tooling
- admin-dashboard/package.json — admin dashboard dev/build/test scripts
